proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\).  By
\texttt{thm:socp-coverage}, an optimizing SOCP weight array and the
deterministic half-widths
\[
 \ell_e=b_e(w)+z_B\operatorname{sd}_e(w) \tag{51}
\]
form an honest band whose maximum half-width is \(\Gamma_s\).  Hence
\[
 W_s\leq\Gamma_s. \tag{52}
\]

For the reverse comparison, take any feasible pair \((w,\ell)\) in
\texttt{def:exact-width-frontier} and put
\[
 R=\max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e. \tag{53}
\]
The nonempty-treated-set domain of \texttt{def:exact-width-frontier} and
\(K\geq0\) imply \(M=|\mathcal E|\geq1\), so this maximum and
\(q_\alpha(M)\) are defined.

First, \(b_e(w)\leq R\) for every \(e\).  Otherwise, for some \(e\), the
endpoint-attainment assertion of \texttt{lem:bias-radius} supplies a
model-class law under which the coordinate error has mean \(b_e(w)>R\).
By \texttt{lem:contrast-geometry}, its variance
\(\operatorname{sd}_e(w)^2\) is positive.  Since \(\ell_e\leq R\), writing
the error as \(b_e(w)+\operatorname{sd}_e(w)G\), with
\(G\sim N(0,1)\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr\{|\widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e|\leq\ell_e\}
 &\leq \Phi\!\left(
 \frac{\ell_e-b_e(w)}{\operatorname{sd}_e(w)}\right)\\
 &<\frac12<1-\alpha.
\end{aligned} \tag{54}
\]
The simultaneous event is contained in this coordinate event, contradicting
uniform honesty.  Therefore
\[
 \max_{e\in\mathcal E}b_e(w)\leq R. \tag{55}
\]
Only coordinatewise endpoint attainment is used in (54); no simultaneous
choice of all bias endpoints is asserted.

We next obtain a stochastic lower bound under one jointly valid model law.
Choose any \(e_0\in\mathcal E\) and any model-class law supplied by the
attainment part of \texttt{lem:bias-radius}.  By
\texttt{lem:prediction-error}, under this law
\[
 \widehat\tau(w)-\tau=\mu+Z,
 \qquad Z\sim N(0,V),
 \qquad V=A(w)\Sigma_QA(w)^{\top}, \tag{56}
\]
for one joint mean vector \(\mu=A(w)m\).  By
\texttt{lem:contrast-geometry},
\[
 V\succeq\sigma_{\min}I_M. \tag{57}
\]
Let \(X\sim N(0,\sigma_{\min}I_M)\), and independently let
\(U\sim N(0,V-\sigma_{\min}I_M)\), permitting a singular covariance for
\(U\).  Then \(X+U\) has the same law as \(Z\).

Write \(s_0=\sqrt{\sigma_{\min}}>0\).  For \(R>0\) and \(u\in\mathbb R\),
define
\[
 g_R(u)=\Pr\{|s_0G+u|\leq R\}
 =\Phi\!\left(\frac{R-u}{s_0}\right)
  +\Phi\!\left(\frac{R+u}{s_0}\right)-1. \tag{58}
\]
This function is even.  For \(u\geq0\),
\[
 g_R'(u)=\frac1{s_0}\left\{
 \varphi\!\left(\frac{R+u}{s_0}\right)
 -\varphi\!\left(\frac{R-u}{s_0}\right)\right\}\leq0, \tag{59}
\]
because \(|R+u|\geq|R-u|\) and the standard normal density decreases with
absolute value.  Hence \(g_R(u)\leq g_R(0)\) for all real \(u\).  Conditional
on \(U=u\), the coordinates of \(X\) are independent, and (58)--(59) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr\{\mu+X+U\in[-R,R]^M\mid U=u\}
 &=\prod_{k=1}^M g_R(u_k+\mu_k)\\
 &\leq g_R(0)^M
 =\Pr\{X\in[-R,R]^M\}.
\end{aligned} \tag{60}
\]
Integration over \(U\) proves the same inequality unconditionally.  At
\(R=0\), both relevant cube probabilities are zero because \(X\) is
nonsingular, so the inequality remains valid.

The coverage rectangle is contained in \([-R,R]^M\).  Uniform honesty under
the particular law in (56), followed by (60), yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 1-\alpha
 &\leq\Pr\{|\widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e|\leq\ell_e
              \text{ for every }e\in\mathcal E\}\\
 &\leq\Pr\{\mu+Z\in[-R,R]^M\}\\
 &\leq\Pr\{X\in[-R,R]^M\}\\
 &=\Pr\left\{\max_{1\leq k\leq M}|G_k|
       \leq\frac{R}{\sqrt{\sigma_{\min}}}\right\},
\end{aligned} \tag{61}
\]
where the last-line variables are independent standard normals.  The final
probability is strictly increasing in its nonnegative threshold.  By the
definition of \(q_\alpha(M)\),
\[
 R\geq\sqrt{\sigma_{\min}}\,q_\alpha(M). \tag{62}
\]

The coordinate upper bound in \texttt{lem:contrast-geometry} and the
dimension-uniform calibration in \texttt{lem:gaussian-quantile-ratio} give
\[
 \operatorname{sd}_e(w)\leq\sqrt{2\sigma_{\max}},
 \qquad
 z_B\leq c_\alpha q_\alpha(M). \tag{63}
\]
Since \(\Gamma_s\) is the minimum SOCP envelope, (55), (62), and (63) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Gamma_s
 &\leq\max_{e\in\mathcal E}
       \{b_e(w)+z_B\operatorname{sd}_e(w)\}\\
 &\leq R+c_\alpha q_\alpha(M)\sqrt{2\sigma_{\max}}\\
 &\leq\left(1+c_\alpha
       \sqrt{\frac{2\sigma_{\max}}{\sigma_{\min}}}\right)R.
\end{aligned} \tag{64}
\]
Taking the infimum over all honest \((w,\ell)\) and combining with (52)
proves
\[
 W_s\leq\Gamma_s\leq
 \left(1+c_\alpha
 \sqrt{\frac{2\sigma_{\max}}{\sigma_{\min}}}\right)W_s.
\]
The denominator is positive by the declared covariance-band parameter domain.
There is no asymptotic condition in this theorem, and its factor is independent
of the panel dimensions, adoption pattern, predictors, and donor-overlap
geometry.

added_lemmas.statement:
For either \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\), the exact robust
deterministic linear-band frontier is attained and satisfies
\[
 W_s=\min_{w\in\mathcal F_s}\ \max_{b\in\mathcal B(w)}
 r_\alpha\!\left(b,A(w)\Sigma_QA(w)^{\top}\right). \tag{15}
\]
For every feasible \(w\), the set \(\mathcal B(w)\) is compact and every one
of its elements is jointly attainable by a law in the declared model class.
The map \((b,V)\mapsto r_\alpha(b,V)\) is well defined and continuous on
\(\mathbb R^M\times\mathbb S_{++}^M\); both the maximum and the minimum in
(15) are therefore attained.  At an optimizing weight array, equal
half-widths equal to the right side of (15) form an honest band.  No
coordinatewise simultaneous endpoint-attainment assumption is required.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\).  The domain condition in
\texttt{def:exact-width-frontier} gives \(\mathcal J\ne\varnothing\), and
therefore \(M=|\mathcal E|\geq1\).  Assumption
\texttt{ass:donor-feasibility} and the inclusion
\(D_{jK}\subseteq D_{jh}\) for \(0\leq h\leq K\) make every coordinate
simplex under either support rule nonempty.  Each such simplex is closed and
bounded in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.  Since \(\mathcal E\) is
finite, their product \(\mathcal F_s\) is nonempty and compact.

We first verify the asserted Gaussian radius.  For
\(b\in\mathbb R^M\), \(V\in\mathbb S_{++}^M\), and \(R\geq0\), put
\[
 H(b,V,R)=\Pr_{Z\sim N(b,V)}\{Z\in[-R,R]^M\}. \tag{16}
\]
The density of \(N(b,V)\) is continuous and strictly positive on all of
\(\mathbb R^M\).  Consequently \(H(b,V,0)=0\),
\(H(b,V,R)\to1\) as \(R\to\infty\), and, whenever
\(0\leq R_1<R_2\),
\[
 H(b,V,R_1)<H(b,V,R_2), \tag{17}
\]
because the difference of the two cubes contains a nonempty open rectangle.
Continuity in \(R\) follows by bounding the probability of the difference
between two nearby cubes by the integral of the bounded Gaussian density over
that difference.  Since \(0<\alpha<1/2\), (16)--(17) give a unique positive
root \(r_\alpha(b,V)\).

This root is jointly continuous.  Indeed, if
\((b_n,V_n)\to(b,V)\) with every \(V_n\) and \(V\) positive definite, then
\(V_n^{-1}\to V^{-1}\) and \(\det(V_n)\to\det(V)>0\).  On every fixed cube,
the corresponding normal densities therefore converge uniformly, so
\[
 H(b_n,V_n,R)\longrightarrow H(b,V,R)
 \quad\text{for every fixed }R\geq0. \tag{18}
\]
Let \(r=r_\alpha(b,V)>0\).  For every \(0<\varepsilon<r\), (17) gives
\[
 H(b,V,r-\varepsilon)<1-\alpha<H(b,V,r+\varepsilon). \tag{19}
\]
By (18), both strict inequalities persist for all sufficiently large \(n\).
The monotonicity and defining uniqueness of the roots then imply
\[
 r-\varepsilon<r_\alpha(b_n,V_n)<r+\varepsilon, \tag{20}
\]
which proves joint continuity.

Let
\[
 \Theta=\left\{(\beta,r):
 \lVert\beta_t\rVert_2\leq L\ (t\in\mathcal T),\quad
 |r_{it}|\leq\delta/2\ ((i,t)\in\mathcal C)\right\}. \tag{21}
\]
This is a nonempty compact finite product of closed Euclidean balls and
closed intervals.  For \(\theta=(\beta,r)\in\Theta\), define
\(m^\theta_{it}=x_i^{\top}\beta_t+r_{it}\).  The map
\[
 (w,\theta)\longmapsto
 \left(A(w)m^\theta,A(w)\Sigma_QA(w)^{\top}\right) \tag{22}
\]
is continuous.  Moreover, \texttt{lem:contrast-geometry} gives the uniform
positive-definiteness condition
\[
 A(w)\Sigma_QA(w)^{\top}\succeq\sigma_{\min}I_M\succ0
 \quad(w\in\mathcal F_s). \tag{23}
\]
It follows from (20)--(23) that
\[
 f(w,\theta)=r_\alpha\!\left(
 A(w)m^\theta,A(w)\Sigma_QA(w)^{\top}\right) \tag{24}
\]
is continuous on the compact set \(\mathcal F_s\times\Theta\).
For fixed \(w\), the image of \(\Theta\) under
\(\theta\mapsto A(w)m^\theta\) is exactly \(\mathcal B(w)\), so this set
is compact and the maximum of (24) over \(\theta\) is attained.  Uniform
continuity of \(f\) on the product compact set gives, for \(w,w'\) close,
\[
 \left|\max_{\theta\in\Theta}f(w,\theta)
       -\max_{\theta\in\Theta}f(w',\theta)\right|
 \leq\max_{\theta\in\Theta}|f(w,\theta)-f(w',\theta)|, \tag{25}
\]
and the right side tends to zero as \(w'\to w\).  Thus the outer objective
in (15) is continuous on \(\mathcal F_s\), and its minimum is attained.

We next establish that \(\mathcal B(w)\) is the exact joint bias set, rather
than merely an envelope.  If \(P\) belongs to
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,K,p}(L,\delta,\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max})\), then
\texttt{ass:mean-structure}, \texttt{ass:coefficient-radius}, and
\texttt{ass:cellwise-misspecification} provide some \(\theta\in\Theta\)
with mean vector \(m=m^\theta\).  Hence
\[
 A(w)m\in\mathcal B(w). \tag{26}
\]
Conversely, take any \(b=A(w)m^\theta\in\mathcal B(w)\).  Let
\(Q\sim N(m^\theta,\Sigma_Q)\), assign its deduplicated coordinates to the
corresponding untreated potential outcomes, define untreated outcomes outside
\(\mathcal C\) arbitrarily, take treated potential outcomes equal to the
untreated ones, and define observed outcomes by
\texttt{ass:consistency}.  The chosen \(\theta\) satisfies each bound in
(21), while the fixed inputs already satisfy the donor and covariance-band
conditions.  This constructs a member of \texttt{def:model-class} whose
joint error mean is exactly \(b\).  Thus every element of \(\mathcal B(w)\)
is jointly attainable.  Notice that this construction respects shared
\(\beta_t\)'s and deduplicated remainders; it never combines separately
attained coordinate endpoints.

By \texttt{lem:prediction-error}, under a model law having bias
\(b=A(w)m\),
\[
 \widehat\tau(w)-\tau\sim
 N\!\left(b,V(w)\right),
 \qquad V(w)=A(w)\Sigma_QA(w)^{\top}. \tag{27}
\]
This is a derived relation between the observed linear contrast and the
realized potential-outcome effect \(\tau\); it does not redefine the causal
target.

Fix \(w\), let \(\ell\in[0,\infty)^M\), and put
\(R=\max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e\).  For every bias vector \(b\),
\[
 \{|Z_e|\leq\ell_e\text{ for every }e\in\mathcal E\}
 \subseteq\{\lVert Z\rVert_\infty\leq R\}. \tag{28}
\]
If \((w,\ell)\) is uniformly honest, joint attainability, (27), and (28)
imply
\[
 H(b,V(w),R)\geq1-\alpha
 \quad\text{for every }b\in\mathcal B(w), \tag{29}
\]
and hence, by (17),
\[
 R\geq\max_{b\in\mathcal B(w)}r_\alpha(b,V(w)). \tag{30}
\]
Conversely, set
\[
 R(w)=\max_{b\in\mathcal B(w)}r_\alpha(b,V(w)) \tag{31}
\]
and choose \(\ell_e=R(w)\) for every \(e\).  Then the rectangle equals the
cube in (28).  Equations (17), (26), (27), and (31) show that its coverage is
at least \(1-\alpha\) under every member of the model class.  Thus (30) is
attainable at fixed \(w\).  Minimizing (31) over the compact feasible set and
using (25) proves (15), including equal-half-width optimality and both
attainment assertions.  All arguments are finite-sample; no boundary
interiority, predictor-rank condition, independent-coordinate bias choice, or
limit passage is used.
added_lemmas.justification: This theorem gives the exact robust frontier for the full declared bounded-mean class by retaining the joint restrictions among bias coordinates.
added_lemmas.gap: Scalar worst-case-bias formulas and zero-bias covariance quantiles do not characterize the jointly attainable shifted Gaussian maximum over staggered donor simplexes.
added_lemmas.consumer: A solver can optimize the displayed finite min--max functional directly or use it as the exact benchmark for the Bonferroni SOCP.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(\alpha\in\mathbb Q\cap(0,1/2)\) and define the finite constant
\[
 C_\alpha=\sqrt{2\log(4/\alpha)}+
 \sqrt{2\log 2+2\log(4/\alpha)}.
\]
For every rational \(\lambda>0\) and integer \(n\geq5\), there is a legal
rational instance with
\(K=0\), \(M_n=2^{n^2}\) treated units adopting in the sole calendar period,
one shared never-treated donor, \(L=\delta=0\),
\(\sigma_{\min,n}=\lambda^2n^{-2}\), and
\(\sigma_{\max,n}=\lambda^2\), such that, for both
support rules and every supplied certified Bonferroni multiplier \(z_{B,n}\),
\[
 W_s\leq C_\alpha\lambda=C_\alpha\sqrt{\sigma_{\max,n}},
 \qquad
 \Gamma_s=z_{B,n}\lambda\sqrt{1+n^{-2}}
 \geq\frac{\lambda}{2}\sqrt{\log M_n}, \tag{32}
\]
and consequently
\[
 \frac{\Gamma_s}{W_s}
 \geq\frac{\sqrt{\log2}}{2C_\alpha}\,n
 =\frac{\sqrt{\log2}}{2C_\alpha}
 \sqrt{\frac{\sigma_{\max,n}}{\sigma_{\min,n}}}. \tag{33}
\]
The deduplicated contrast covariance in this family is
\(\lambda^2(n^{-2}I_{M_n}+\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\top})\).  Hence the square-root
condition-number dependence in \texttt{thm:constant-factor-frontier} is
order-sharp, up to constants depending only on \(\alpha\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix rational \(\lambda>0\), fix \(n\geq5\), and write \(M=2^{n^2}\).
Take \(T=1\), \(K=0\),
\(N=M+1\), and \(p=1\).  Label the first \(M\) units by
\(j=1,\ldots,M\), give each adoption date \(T_j=1\), and let
\(d=M+1\) be the sole never-treated unit, with \(T_d=\infty\).  Set
\(x_i=0\) for every unit and \(L=\delta=0\).  Then
\[
 \mathcal J=\{1,\ldots,M\},\qquad
 \mathcal E=\{(j,0):1\leq j\leq M\},\qquad
 D_{j0}=\{d\}. \tag{34}
\]
Thus donor feasibility and nonvacuity hold, the nested and deep feasible sets
coincide, and every contrast weight is forced to put mass one on \(d\).

After deduplication, the cell set is exactly
\[
 \mathcal C=\{(j,1):1\leq j\leq M\}\cup\{(d,1)\}; \tag{35}
\]
in particular, the common donor cell occurs only once.  In this ordering let
\[
 R_Q=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda n^{-1}I_M,\lambda),
 \qquad
 \Sigma_Q=R_Q^{\top}R_Q
 =\operatorname{diag}(\lambda^2n^{-2}I_M,\lambda^2). \tag{36}
\]
The factor is nonsingular and rational.  Its covariance obeys
\[
 \lambda^2n^{-2}I_{M+1}\preceq\Sigma_Q
 \preceq\lambda^2I_{M+1}, \tag{37}
\]
so the declared spectral band holds with
\(\sigma_{\min,n}=\lambda^2n^{-2}\) and
\(\sigma_{\max,n}=\lambda^2\).  This verifies that
the construction is a legal deduplicated fixed design in the model class.

Because \(L=\delta=0\), the attainable bias set is the singleton
\(\{0\}\).  Let \(U\sim N(0,\lambda^2)\) be the donor-cell noise and let
\(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_M\) be independent
\(N(0,\lambda^2n^{-2})\) treated-cell noises, also independent of \(U\).
From the
rows \(a_j=\mathbf e_j-\mathbf e_d\), the error vector has the representation
\[
 Z=(\varepsilon_1-U,\ldots,\varepsilon_M-U),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(Z)=\lambda^2
 (n^{-2}I_M+\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\top}). \tag{38}
\]
By \texttt{thm:attainable-bias-exact-frontier}, both support rules have the
same exact width, namely the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of
\(\max_j|\varepsilon_j-U|\).

We give a finite upper bound for that quantile.  If \(G\sim N(0,1)\), then
completing the square in its density gives
\(\mathbb E e^{tG}=e^{t^2/2}\).  On \(\{G\geq t\}\),
\(1\leq e^{tG-t^2}\); integration and symmetry therefore give, for
\(t\geq0\),
\[
 \Pr\{G\geq t\}\leq e^{-t^2/2},
 \qquad
 \Pr\{|G|\geq t\}\leq2e^{-t^2/2}. \tag{39}
\]
Put
\[
 t_0=\lambda\sqrt{2\log(4/\alpha)},
 \qquad
 t_1=\frac{\lambda}{n}\sqrt{2\log(4M/\alpha)}. \tag{40}
\]
Equation (39) and a union bound yield
\[
 \Pr\{|U|>t_0\}\leq\alpha/2,
 \qquad
 \Pr\{\max_j|\varepsilon_j|>t_1\}\leq\alpha/2. \tag{41}
\]
On the complementary event,
\(\max_j|\varepsilon_j-U|\leq t_0+t_1\).  Since
\(\log M=n^2\log2\),
\[
 t_1=\lambda\sqrt{2\log2+\frac{2}{n^2}\log(4/\alpha)}
 \leq\lambda\sqrt{2\log2+2\log(4/\alpha)}. \tag{42}
\]
Equations (40)--(42) and the exact characterization therefore prove
\[
 W_{\mathrm{nested}}=W_{\mathrm{deep}}\leq C_\alpha\lambda. \tag{43}
\]

For the SOCP, every contrast has zero bias and standard deviation
\[
 \operatorname{sd}_j=\lambda\sqrt{1+n^{-2}}. \tag{44}
\]
There is no weight choice, and taking the norm epigraph variables at equality
is feasible.  Thus \texttt{def:bonferroni-socp} gives exactly
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}
 =z_{B,n}\lambda\sqrt{1+n^{-2}}. \tag{45}
\]
The certified tail inequality for \(z_{B,n}\) and strict monotonicity of
\(\Phi\) imply
\[
 z_{B,n}\geq\Phi^{-1}\!\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2M}\right). \tag{46}
\]

It remains to give an explicit lower bound for this Gaussian quantile.  Let
\(\varphi\) be the standard normal density, put
\(x=\tfrac12\sqrt{\log M}\), and note that
\(\log M=n^2\log2>16\) for \(n\geq5\).  Since \(\varphi\) decreases on
\([0,\infty)\),
\[
 1-\Phi(x)=\int_x^\infty\varphi(u)\,du
 \geq\int_x^{x+1}\varphi(u)\,du
 \geq\varphi(x+1). \tag{47}
\]
For \(\log M\geq16\),
\[
 \frac{(x+1)^2}{2}
 =\frac18\log M+\frac12\sqrt{\log M}+\frac12
 \leq\frac38\log M. \tag{48}
\]
Consequently
\[
 1-\Phi(x)
 \geq(2\pi)^{-1/2}M^{-3/8}
 >\frac{\alpha}{2M}, \tag{49}
\]
where the last inequality follows from \(M\geq1\), \(\alpha<1/2\), and
\(2/\sqrt{2\pi}>1/2\).  Equations (46)--(49) show that
\[
 z_{B,n}\geq\frac12\sqrt{\log M}. \tag{50}
\]
Combining (43), (45), and (50) gives (32)--(33), because
\(\log M=n^2\log2\) and
\(\sqrt{\sigma_{\max,n}/\sigma_{\min,n}}=n\).  Thus a common donor keeps the
exact Gaussian maximum at order \(\sqrt{\sigma_{\max,n}}\), while fixed
Bonferroni calibration pays \(\sqrt{\log M}\); along this legal family the
latter equals a constant times the square root of the covariance condition
number.  The statement is finite for every \(n\), and only the final
order-sharp conclusion takes \(n\to\infty\).
added_lemmas.justification: The legal common-donor family proves that the square-root spectral condition-number factor is a genuine worst-case price of fixed Bonferroni calibration, not an artifact of the upper-bound proof.
added_lemmas.gap: The cited synthetic-control and scalar interval comparators do not give an order-sharp ratio between a simultaneous Bonferroni conic band and the exact robust rectangular-width frontier.
added_lemmas.consumer: Users of the SOCP can interpret a large condition-number factor as unavoidable in general while still assessing whether their particular covariance has a much smaller exact Gaussian-max calibration.

proposed_core_edits.name: BiasSet
proposed_core_edits.reason: The all-bias exact frontier requires a named set that preserves the joint restrictions imposed by shared calendar-time coefficients and deduplicated remainders.

proposed_core_edits.name: rShiftAlpha
proposed_core_edits.reason: The full-class exact frontier needs the shifted, rather than only centered, Gaussian-cube radius.

proposed.name: Attainable joint contrast-bias set
proposed.construction:
For a feasible weight array \(w\), let
\[
 \mathcal B(w)=\left\{A(w)m^{\beta,r}:
 \begin{array}{l}
 \beta=(\beta_t)_{t\in\mathcal T},\quad
 r=(r_{it})_{(i,t)\in\mathcal C},\\
 \lVert\beta_t\rVert_2\leq L\text{ for every }t\in\mathcal T,\quad
 |r_{it}|\leq\delta/2\text{ for every }(i,t)\in\mathcal C,\\
 m^{\beta,r}_{it}=x_i^{\top}\beta_t+r_{it}
 \text{ for every }(i,t)\in\mathcal C
 \end{array}\right\}\subseteq\mathbb R^M.
\]
Thus \(\mathcal B(w)\) preserves all sharing restrictions induced by a common
calendar-time coefficient and by deduplicated cells; no Cartesian-product
relaxation of its coordinatewise projections is made.
inputs: the common coefficient and cellwise remainder restrictions

proposed_core_edits.reason: Coordinatewise bias endpoints need not be jointly attainable, so exact robustness must optimize over the image of the common nuisance parameter set.

proposed.name: Shifted Gaussian-cube radius
proposed.construction:
For \(b\in\mathbb R^M\) and \(V\in\mathbb S_{++}^M\), define
\(r_\alpha(b,V)\) as the unique \(R\in(0,\infty)\) satisfying
\[
 \Pr_{Z\sim N(b,V)}\{\lVert Z\rVert_\infty\leq R\}=1-\alpha.
\]
Existence, uniqueness, and continuity on
\(\mathbb R^M\times\mathbb S_{++}^M\) are asserted and proved in
\texttt{thm:attainable-bias-exact-frontier}.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This construction is the computable fixed-weight robust radius used by the exact full-class variational characterization.

prose_updates.tldr: Staggered adoption creates shrinking not-yet-treated donor sets. Conditional on the declared nonempty rational fixed design, this note maps every treated-unit--horizon error into one deduplicated Gaussian contrast vector and defines the jointly attainable bias set generated by the shared calendar-time coefficients and cellwise remainder bounds. The exact honest deterministic linear-band frontier is the attained minimum, over the relevant product of donor simplexes, of the worst shifted Gaussian-cube radius over that joint bias set. A fixed-Bonferroni bias-plus-standard-error SOCP remains finite-sample honest and within the stated dimension-uniform spectral factor of this exact frontier. A legal common-donor family with rational covariance factor proves that the square-root covariance-condition-number dependence is order-sharp for fixed Bonferroni calibration. Zero-bias Loewner and diagonal row-disjoint results still give computable strict nested-width gains, while the facial-reduction theorem separately certifies strict improvement of the SOCP surrogate on degenerate faces. Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein provide donor geometry only; \texttt{scpi} and \texttt{augsynth::multisynth} are implementation consumers, not estimators covered by these theorems.

project_justification.gap: Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein define the shrinking donor geometry and discuss deepest-pool and horizon-varying choices, but they do not supply this note's bounded-mean known-covariance experiment or an honest-width frontier for their partially pooled estimator. Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba, and Titiunik provide non-asymptotic simultaneous prediction and conic architecture, but not the exact min--max shifted Gaussian-cube frontier over jointly constrained biases or an order-sharp comparison with fixed Bonferroni calibration. Scalar convex-class interval theory does not resolve the simultaneous correlated rectangle or its donor-support comparison.
project_justification.niche: Known covariance in a prespecified positive spectral band, rational fixed inputs, a nonempty treated set, and this note's bounded linear conditional-mean class define a finite-sample decision problem in which donor availability, shared-cell covariance, joint bias attainability, multiplicity, and exact width are all explicit. The targets are the exact robust frontier \(W_s\), the implementable fixed-Bonferroni SOCP value \(\Gamma_s\), strict nested-support comparisons on proved domains, and the worst-case price of the Bonferroni surrogate.
project_justification.fill: The note derives the deduplicated Gaussian contrast law and exact coordinate bias support function, proves finite-sample SOCP coverage, and characterizes the full bounded-mean frontier as an attained minimum over weights of a maximum shifted Gaussian-cube radius over the joint attainable bias set. It proves the earlier spectral comparison and constructs a legal common-donor sequence on which the SOCP-to-exact-width ratio grows as the square root of the covariance condition number. Separate zero-bias Loewner, independent-coordinate product-root, rational witness, and degeneracy-safe facial-reduction results identify when nested supports strictly improve the exact frontier or its SOCP surrogate.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no random nuisance estimation: weights and half-widths depend only on fixed design and model inputs. For general \(L\) and \(\delta\), exact robustness maximizes the shifted Gaussian-cube radius over the compact joint image of the shared coefficient balls and cellwise remainder box; it does not combine coordinatewise bias endpoints. Correlated Gaussian probability evaluation and numerical max calibration remain post-solve computational refinements. The fixed-Bonferroni SOCP is the directly conic implementation, and the diagonal row-disjoint zero-bias specialization reduces exact calibration to one product equation.

prose_updates.related_work: Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2022, Section 2) supply the shrinking not-yet-treated donor-set geometry and note that their estimator may use horizon-varying donors even though their exposition and application focus on a common deepest pool. They do not supply this note's bounded-mean known-covariance class, and no theorem here evaluates their partially pooled estimator. Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba, and Titiunik (2025, Sections 4.4 and 6 and Supplemental Appendix S.6) provide staggered prediction-error, simultaneous-coverage, and conic-programming architecture; they do not give the joint attainable-bias min--max frontier or the order-sharp SOCP-to-frontier ratio proved here. Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, equation (13) and Sections 3.2--3.4) provide scalar worst-case-bias plus standard-error logic over a convex Gaussian regression class. Anderson (1955, Theorem 1) supplies the weak moving-set inequality used by the separate strict zero-bias Loewner result. Kallus (2020) motivates the dual-norm bias--variance optimization analogy. Pataki (2013) and Jeyakumar, Kum, and Lee (2008) support the separate degeneracy-safe conic certificate. The present results retain the declared known-covariance experiment; they do not claim a covariance-estimation or published-class transfer theorem. \texttt{scpi} and \texttt{augsynth::multisynth} are named as potential software consumers of the geometry and optimization, not as covered procedures.
prose_updates.interpretation: The exact full-class formula keeps the bias coordinates coupled through common calendar-time coefficients and deduplicated cell remainders. This matters because the endpoint attaining one coordinate's bias need not attain all other endpoints simultaneously; the robust width is therefore a maximum over the attainable joint image, not over a Cartesian bias box. In the order-sharp family, every treated contrast shares one donor shock while its treated-cell shock is independent and much smaller. The shared shock keeps the exact Gaussian maximum bounded on the donor-noise scale even when the number of treated units is exponential in the covariance condition number, whereas fixed Bonferroni calibration still pays a square-root log-multiplicity factor. The earlier strict witness continues to isolate the value of an early donor that remains untreated only at the early horizon. These conclusions concern deterministic linear bands in the declared experiment, not the numerical output or statistical class of an existing synthetic-control estimator.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact full-class characterization is a finite-dimensional attained min--max functional, but evaluating correlated shifted Gaussian-cube probabilities and globally optimizing that generally nonconic objective can be computationally harder than solving the Bonferroni SOCP. The order-sharp family shows that the square-root spectral condition-number loss of fixed Bonferroni calibration cannot be removed uniformly, although particular covariance and donor geometries may yield a much smaller gap. The covariance remains known and prespecified; covariance estimation, selective donor choice, outcome-dependent weights, and transfer to a published estimator class are outside this version. The facial-reduction equivalence concerns strict \(\Gamma\) improvement on arbitrary degenerate faces and is not a general strict-\(W\) criterion.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Finite-sample SOCP coverage, the exact full bounded-mean attainable-bias frontier, the covariance-domination sandwich, its square-root condition-number order-sharpness, weak nested-support dominance, and the rational strict witnesses are theorem-level results. The exact formula uses all existing \(L\) and \(\delta\) values and maximizes over the jointly attainable bias set; it does not assume simultaneous coordinatewise endpoint attainment. On the zero-bias class, \texttt{thm:correlated-gaussian-exact-frontier} additionally gives a strict Loewner covariance criterion, while \texttt{thm:disjoint-diagonal-exact-frontier} gives the explicit product root. The complete finite certificate \texttt{thm:degenerate-iff-gap-certificate} concerns strict SOCP improvement on degenerate faces. Unknown covariance, covariance confidence sets, random donor selection, outcome-dependent weights, direct coverage claims for the Ben-Michael--Feller--Rothstein estimator, and coverage claims for \texttt{scpi} or \texttt{augsynth::multisynth} are outside the paper. Correlated Gaussian-max numerical calibration is a post-solve refinement.

statement_notes.justification: The finite-sample sandwich makes the conic band decision-theoretically interpretable, and \texttt{thm:condition-number-order-sharpness} proves that its square-root spectral dependence is unavoidable for fixed Bonferroni calibration.
statement_notes.gap: Armstrong and Kolesar analyze scalar linear functionals, while Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba, and Titiunik do not compare a staggered simultaneous Bonferroni SOCP with the exact robust deterministic linear-rectangle frontier or establish the sharp spectral order.
statement_notes.consumer: Practitioners can use the tractable SOCP with a proved finite-sample frontier guarantee and can interpret the condition-number factor using the matching common-donor lower family; this does not assert coverage for an existing software estimator.

statement_notes.justification: This is the full-class exact characterization: it retains the joint nuisance geometry, proves all min--max and quantile attainment claims, and derives equal-half-width optimality from the honest-band problem.
statement_notes.gap: The comparator literature does not provide this shifted correlated Gaussian-cube optimization over horizon-adaptive versus deepest-pool simplex products with jointly constrained bias vectors.
statement_notes.consumer: The formula is an exact benchmark for numerical Gaussian-max calibration and for assessing the conservatism of the SOCP used in \texttt{scpi}- or \texttt{augsynth::multisynth}-adjacent workflows.

statement_notes.justification: A fully legal rational staggered-panel sequence certifies the lower order matching the spectral dependence of the general SOCP comparison.
statement_notes.gap: No cited comparator establishes this simultaneous fixed-Bonferroni versus exact-width condition-number lower family.
statement_notes.consumer: The theorem separates unavoidable worst-case Bonferroni conservatism from instance-specific opportunities for correlated Gaussian-max refinement.
